chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Muhammad al-Ansari, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from his father, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me:

O Aba al-Miqdam! Indeed, the followers of Ali (peace be upon him) are those who are pale and emaciated, whose lips are withered, whose bellies are thin, whose complexions have changed, and whose faces are yellow. When night falls, they take the earth as a bed, and face the earth with their foreheads. They prostrate frequently, shed tears frequently, make supplication frequently, and cry frequently. And the people rejoice while they are sad.
ai.seo_question: What are the physical and spiritual signs of true Shia followers according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) defines the 'Shiite' not merely by lineage but by the visible marks of *zuhd* (asceticism) and *muraqabah* (God-consciousness), where physical pallor and emaciation result from prolonged night prayers (*qiyam*). This description highlights the dialectic of 'joy in sorrow,' where the true followers find spiritual ecstasy in worship while the world remains oblivious, a concept deeply rooted in Shia eschatological and spiritual traditions. The emphasis on 'changing colors' and 'pale faces' serves as a tangible sign of their distinct identity amidst the general populace.
